sources.title: Unity Biotechnology Announces 12-Week Data for UBX0101 Phase 2
supports: no dose showed statistically significant improvement over placebo at 12 weeks
company discontinued development of UBX0101 for osteoarthritis
sources.limits: First-party disclosure of a negative trial. Useful for the program outcome, not for broad conclusions about senolytics as a class.

sources.title: Senolytics decrease senescent cells in humans: Preliminary report from a clinical trial of Dasatinib plus Quercetin in individuals with diabetic kidney disease
supports: reductions in senescence-associated cell and inflammatory markers after a short D+Q course
sources.limits: No placebo control and too small to establish clinical efficacy or durable health benefit. Best treated as proof of mechanism.

sources.title: Senolytics dasatinib and quercetin in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: results of a phase I, single-blind, single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled pilot trial on feasibility and tolerability
supports: 12 participants randomized to D+Q or placebo
all participants completed dosing and assessments
more non-serious adverse events in the D+Q arm; no serious adverse event attributed to treatment
sources.limits: Tiny pilot designed around feasibility and tolerability rather than efficacy. Investigators disclosed senolytic-related patent interests held by Mayo Clinic.

sources.title: Effects of intermittent senolytic therapy on bone metabolism in postmenopausal women: a phase 2 randomized controlled trial
supports: primary 20-week CTx endpoint did not differ between D+Q and control
exploratory signals in participants with higher baseline senescent-cell burden
sources.limits: Overall primary endpoint was negative; subgroup findings were exploratory. Several investigators disclosed financial interests in senolytic patents and uses held by Mayo Clinic.

sources.title: A pilot study of senolytics to improve cognition and mobility in older adults at risk for Alzheimer's disease
supports: human senolytic testing in older adults at risk for Alzheimer disease
exploratory cognition, mobility, safety and biomarker outcomes
sources.limits: Pilot-scale study, insufficient to establish that senolytic treatment prevents or slows Alzheimer disease or broadly improves aging outcomes.

sources.title: Protocol for a pilot clinical trial of the senolytic drug combination Dasatinib Plus Quercetin to mitigate age-related health and cognitive decline in mental disorders
supports: ongoing expansion of D+Q testing into additional aging-associated clinical populations
trial remains focused on feasibility, safety and exploratory health/cognitive outcomes
sources.limits: Protocol only; it provides no efficacy result and should not be cited as evidence that the treatment works.
